Decision [rust-lang-rust-revert-149375]
Context: Perform many const checks in typeck
Chosen: Perform many const checks in typeck
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #154930: Revert performing basic const checks in typeck on stable
Why it was not used: It was reverted because it unintentionally produced compilation errors for constants in unreachable code, which requires a formal approval process first.
Evidence: PR #149375 / revert PR #154930

Decision [rust-lang-rust-revert-148937]
Context: Remove initialized-bytes tracking from `BorrowedBuf` and `BorrowedCursor`
Chosen: Remove initialized-bytes tracking from `BorrowedBuf` and `BorrowedCursor`
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #150096: Revert #148937
Why it was not used: The change was reverted because it degraded performance by forcing reused memory buffers to undergo redundant re-initialization across repeated read operations.
Evidence: PR #148937 / revert PR #150096

Decision [rust-lang-rust-revert-149060]
Context: early return on duplicate span lowerings
Chosen: early return on duplicate span lowerings
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #149757: Revert "early return on duplicate span lowerings"
Why it was not used: The change was rolled back because it introduced unexpectedly severe compiler performance slowdowns.
Evidence: PR #149060 / revert PR #149757

Decision [rust-lang-rust-revert-149516]
Context: Stop adding MSYS2 to PATH
Chosen: Stop adding MSYS2 to PATH
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #149600: Revert #149516 to fix i686-pc-windows-gnu host
Why it was not used: The change was reverted because it led distribution builds to include an incompatible 64-bit threading library, breaking the 32-bit Windows toolchain.
Evidence: PR #149516 / revert PR #149600

Decision [rust-lang-rust-revert-142034]
Context: Detect method not being present that is present in other tuple types
Chosen: Detect method not being present that is present in other tuple types
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #145765: Revert suggestions for missing methods in tuples
Why it was not used: The feature was backed out because it triggered compiler crashes during diagnostic output that affected stable builds, necessitating a rollback while a permanent resolution is developed.
Evidence: PR #142034 / revert PR #145765

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-140448]
Context: client-go: prevent unbounded goroutine growth in EventBroadcaster
Chosen: client-go: prevent unbounded goroutine growth in EventBroadcaster
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #140990: Revert "client-go: prevent unbounded goroutine growth in EventBroadcaster"
Why it was not used: The commit was rolled back because the subsequent patch carried too much risk right before the release candidate milestone.
Evidence: PR #140448 / revert PR #140990

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-306]
Context: Solved data races in pkg/registry
Chosen: Solved data races in pkg/registry
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #140294: Bump SMD to v6.4.2 to revert #306 to fix regression in SSA for nullable container types
Why it was not used: The change was rolled back because it introduced a server-side apply bug that caused valid list and map updates to fail with unexpected 422 validation errors.
Evidence: PR #306 / revert PR #140294

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-136254]
Context: Extend PostFilterResult with a list of victim Pods
Chosen: Extend PostFilterResult with a list of victim Pods
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #137662: Revert "Extend PostFilterResult with a list of victim Pods"
Why it was not used: The update was reverted because delayed preemption was removed from the 1.36 roadmap, making the additional architectural complexity pointless.
Evidence: PR #136254 / revert PR #137662

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-126794]
Context: Add e2e test for Regular Container image change
Chosen: Add e2e test for Regular Container image change
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #130965: Revert "Add e2e test for Regular Container image change"
Why it was not used: The change was rolled back because it caused failures in the main branch's release-blocking test suite.
Evidence: PR #126794 / revert PR #130965

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-127300]
Context: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] kubelet: Propagate error in doPodResizeAction() to the caller
Chosen: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] kubelet: Propagate error in doPodResizeAction() to the caller
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #128694: Revert "[FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] kubelet: Propagate error in doPodResizeAction() to the caller"
Why it was not used: The commit was reverted because it caused cgroup configuration to constantly trigger errors, which broke the vast majority of pod resizing attempts.
Evidence: PR #127300 / revert PR #128694

Decision [elastic-elasticsearch-revert-154503]
Context: Consolidate fallback storage routing logic into central location
Chosen: Consolidate fallback storage routing logic into central location
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #156367: Revert "Consolidate fallback storage routing logic into central location" and unmute tests
Why it was not used: The change was reverted because it caused multiple test suite failures that required muting.
Evidence: PR #154503 / revert PR #156367

Decision [elastic-elasticsearch-revert-152050]
Context: Remove global ordinals from composite keyword path
Chosen: Remove global ordinals from composite keyword path
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #152553: Revert composite keyword segment-ordinals path
Why it was not used: The change was rolled back because it introduced an unintended system regression.
Evidence: PR #152050 / revert PR #152553

Decision [elastic-elasticsearch-revert-151875]
Context: Use a bulk scorer for rescoring vectors
Chosen: Use a bulk scorer for rescoring vectors
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #152097: Revert "Use a bulk scorer for rescoring vectors"
Why it was not used: It was reverted because certain test seeds triggered failures by attempting to read from an already depleted iterator, with the underlying cause being unclear.
Evidence: PR #151875 / revert PR #152097

Decision [elastic-elasticsearch-revert-120214]
Context: [TEST] Use Docker Compose v2 for TestFixturePlugin
Chosen: [TEST] Use Docker Compose v2 for TestFixturePlugin
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #120294: Revert "[TEST] Use Docker Compose v2 for TestFixturePlugin"
Why it was not used: The change triggered test failures on AmazonLinux 2023, and the Docker version conflict was resolved directly inside the virtual machine images instead.
Evidence: PR #120214 / revert PR #120294

Decision [elastic-elasticsearch-revert-147071]
Context: Enforce single values for text fields and ip fields when multi_value=no is configured in the mapping (multi_value=no part 3/5)
Chosen: Enforce single values for text fields and ip fields when multi_value=no is configured in the mapping (multi_value=no part 3/5)
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #147360: Revert "Enforce single values when multi_value=no is configured on fields with doc values (#147071)"
Why it was not used: It was reverted because faulty feature gating caused new tests to fail on mixed-version clusters and break the CI pipeline.
Evidence: PR #147071 / revert PR #147360

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Automatic bucket mounting to Pods
Why it was not used: Application connection methods vary too widely to create a unified mount implementation across all storage drivers.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: BucketAccess credentials as a single JSON blob
Why it was not used: Driver authors found monolithic JSON files difficult to parse and requested discrete key-value fields for flexible injection.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Finalizers for cross-resource protection
Why it was not used: Admins frequently delete finalizers when troubleshooting, leading to broken cluster states and improper driver cleanup.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Creation tracking annotation for buckets
Why it was not used: The mechanism was deemed unnecessary for COSI, though it could be introduced later as an internal implementation detail.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: BucketClass reference on Bucket resources
Why it was not used: Binding control is handled adequately via BucketClaim references, making class tracking on the Bucket redundant.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Preventing updates to existing BucketAccess Secrets
Why it was not used: It prevents administrators from rotating credentials and stops systems from updating endpoint details when locations change.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Static provisioning for BucketAccess
Why it was not used: Supporting varied driver access policies would create extreme complexity, specification ambiguity, and high bug risks.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Unified data and metadata read/write permission
Why it was not used: Administrators would be unable to restrict access to behavior-altering bucket metadata while granting data permissions.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Data-only read/write permission mode
Why it was not used: Storage drivers would be forced to implement metadata permission handling individually via custom class parameters.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Separate credential Secret for multi-bucket access
Why it was not used: It breaks parity with the standard 1:1 workflow by requiring users to manage an additional Secret for shared credentials.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Two output secrets for standard single-bucket access
Why it was not used: Splitting bucket metadata and credentials into two secrets adds unnecessary complexity and confusion to the basic use case.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Separate MultiBucketAccess CRD
Why it was not used: The usability benefit did not justify the architectural overhead and added specification complexity of a new CRD.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Dropping multi-bucket access support
Why it was not used: Multi-bucket access was consistently the most requested feature from users across COSI and ObjectBucketClaim.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: gRPC capability negotiation for multi-bucket support
Why it was not used: Documenting and reporting the complex permutations of drivers, backend types, and auth methods in gRPC was infeasible.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1979-object-storage-support]
Context: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Chosen: KEP-1979: Object Storage Support
Alternative considered: Separate DriverGrantMultipleBucketAccess gRPC call
Why it was not used: This was deferred because the existing bucket access gRPC method is not currently overloaded.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1979-object-storage-support/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-1205-bound-service-account-tokens]
Context: Bound Service Account Tokens
Chosen: Bound Service Account Tokens
Alternative considered: Per-user ID volumes
Why it was not used: Requires complex kubelet re-architecting to inspect image user directives, handle mutable image tags, and manage separate volume mounts.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/1205-bound-service-account-tokens/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-1205-bound-service-account-tokens]
Context: Bound Service Account Tokens
Chosen: Bound Service Account Tokens
Alternative considered: Random fsGroup assignment
Why it was not used: It risks conflicting with existing group configurations and potentially degrading security.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/1205-bound-service-account-tokens/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-1205-bound-service-account-tokens]
Context: Bound Service Account Tokens
Chosen: Bound Service Account Tokens
Alternative considered: World-readable token files
Why it was not used: It introduces security drawbacks referenced earlier in the document.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/1205-bound-service-account-tokens/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-2718-20210511-client-exec-proxy]
Context: KEP-2718: Client Executable Proxy
Chosen: KEP-2718: Client Executable Proxy
Alternative considered: Request Replacement
Why it was not used: Specifying the custom request-response protocol was deemed overly cumbersome, lacked flexibility for broader proxy scenarios, and could not support TLS offloading.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/2718-20210511-client-exec-proxy/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-cloud-provider-2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider]
Context: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Chosen: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Alternative considered: API Server Proxy
Why it was not used: It was out of scope, lacked clear user demand, and designing it would delay the extraction of in-tree cloud providers.
Evidence: keps/sig-cloud-provider/2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-cloud-provider-2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider]
Context: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Chosen: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Alternative considered: Sidecar Credential Daemon
Why it was not used: Operating a persistent daemon per node adds unnecessary complexity compared to simply executing a binary.
Evidence: keps/sig-cloud-provider/2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-cloud-provider-2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider]
Context: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Chosen: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Alternative considered: Bound Service Account Token Flow
Why it was not used: Deferred as a potential future improvement because it falls outside the objective of extracting cloud provider code.
Evidence: keps/sig-cloud-provider/2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-cloud-provider-2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider]
Context: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Chosen: Out-of-Tree Credential Providers
Alternative considered: Pushing Credential Management into the CRI
Why it was not used: Deferred for future consideration because it requires a substantial redesign and is outside the current scope.
Evidence: keps/sig-cloud-provider/2133-out-of-tree-credential-provider/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-2332-pruning-for-custom-resources]
Context: Pruning for Custom Resources
Chosen: Pruning for Custom Resources
Alternative considered: Skeleton schema approach
Why it was not used: It was rejected due to complex semantics, whereas structural schemas naturally mirror Go struct generation and standard unmarshalling behavior.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/2332-pruning-for-custom-resources/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-2332-pruning-for-custom-resources]
Context: Pruning for Custom Resources
Chosen: Pruning for Custom Resources
Alternative considered: Nested re-enabling of pruning via x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: false
Why it was not used: This approach was deferred because clear use cases are currently lacking and it could encourage non-idiomatic API designs.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/2332-pruning-for-custom-resources/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-2332-pruning-for-custom-resources]
Context: Pruning for Custom Resources
Chosen: Pruning for Custom Resources
Alternative considered: Per-version pruning configuration in CustomResourceDefinitionVersion
Why it was not used: It was rejected because inconsistent pruning across versions undermines data consistency and security.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/2332-pruning-for-custom-resources/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-2332-pruning-for-custom-resources]
Context: Pruning for Custom Resources
Chosen: Pruning for Custom Resources
Alternative considered: Recursive additionalProperties semantics instead of a vendor extension
Why it was not used: It was rejected because OpenAPI v3 schema constructs do not operate recursively, so this would violate OpenAPI conventions.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/2332-pruning-for-custom-resources/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-api-machinery-2332-pruning-for-custom-resources]
Context: Pruning for Custom Resources
Chosen: Pruning for Custom Resources
Alternative considered: Pruning when additionalProperties is set to false
Why it was not used: It was rejected because evaluating schema emptiness is computationally infeasible and conflates value validation with structural operations.
Evidence: keps/sig-api-machinery/2332-pruning-for-custom-resources/README.md

Decision [rust-lang-rust-revert-144407]
Context: fix(debuginfo): disable overflow check for recursive non-enum types
Chosen: fix(debuginfo): disable overflow check for recursive non-enum types
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #145979: Revert "fix(debuginfo): disable overflow check for recursive non-enum types"
Why it was not used: The compiler team decided during triage to roll back the PR rather than try to resolve its issues with a forward patch.
Evidence: PR #144407 / revert PR #145979

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-129701]
Context: tests: include stdout of failed commands in JUnit
Chosen: tests: include stdout of failed commands in JUnit
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #129769: Revert "tests: include stdout of failed commands in JUnit"
Why it was not used: The change was reverted because it disrupted TestGrid's result processing, likely due to unsupported characters in the output.
Evidence: PR #129701 / revert PR #129769

Decision [kubernetes-kubernetes-revert-126599]
Context: fix: preserve options after remount for bind mounting
Chosen: fix: preserve options after remount for bind mounting
Rejected/Reverted: reverted in #127899: Revert 126599: fix: preserve options after remount for bind mounting
Why it was not used: The pull request was rolled back because it introduced regressions that caused automated GCE COS test suites to fail.
Evidence: PR #126599 / revert PR #127899

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-279-limit-node-access]
Context: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Chosen: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Alternative considered: File or flag-based apiserver configuration
Why it was not used: It increases operational complexity, creates inconsistency across clusters, and is difficult to inspect or synchronize in high-availability setups.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/279-limit-node-access/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-279-limit-node-access]
Context: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Chosen: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Alternative considered: API-based apiserver configuration
Why it was not used: It reduces behavioral consistency across clusters and creates a potential privilege escalation vector if a node is compromised.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/279-limit-node-access/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-279-limit-node-access]
Context: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Chosen: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Alternative considered: Permissive labeling with NoSchedule taints for violations
Why it was not used: It introduced excessive complexity by requiring an extra cleanup controller and made tracking which labels triggered the taint difficult.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/279-limit-node-access/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-279-limit-node-access]
Context: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Chosen: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
Alternative considered: Forbidding all labels across all namespaces except an allowlist
Why it was not used: It would disrupt existing node-label workflows, hinder integrations like CSI that use custom topology labels, and inappropriately limit non-Kubernetes namespaces.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/279-limit-node-access/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-2451-service-account-token-volumes]
Context: Service Account Token Volumes [Replaced by [Bound Service Account Tokens](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/1205-bound-service-account-tokens)]
Chosen: Service Account Token Volumes [Replaced by [Bound Service Account Tokens](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/1205-bound-service-account-tokens)]
Alternative considered: Flex volume or CSI plugin
Why it was not used: Both storage plugins were still experimental, lacked support in some virtual kubelet environments, and tokens are too foundational to delegate.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/2451-service-account-token-volumes/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-2451-service-account-token-volumes]
Context: Service Account Token Volumes [Replaced by [Bound Service Account Tokens](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/1205-bound-service-account-tokens)]
Chosen: Service Account Token Volumes [Replaced by [Bound Service Account Tokens](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/1205-bound-service-account-tokens)]
Alternative considered: Removing service accounts from core
Why it was not used: Other core features depend on service accounts, so moving them out-of-tree would unnecessarily complicate installation for most users.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/2451-service-account-token-volumes/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-cli-2382-kustomize-exec-secret-generator]
Context: Kustomize Exec Secret Generator
Chosen: Kustomize Exec Secret Generator
Alternative considered: Git-style plugins
Why it was not used: Interactive subcommand interfaces are unnecessary because plugins are meant to be executed declaratively.
Evidence: keps/sig-cli/2382-kustomize-exec-secret-generator/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-cli-2382-kustomize-exec-secret-generator]
Context: Kustomize Exec Secret Generator
Chosen: Kustomize Exec Secret Generator
Alternative considered: Environment variable plugin activation
Why it was not used: Using an environment variable offers little security improvement over relying on plugin directory locations.
Evidence: keps/sig-cli/2382-kustomize-exec-secret-generator/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-instrumentation-647-apiserver-tracing]
Context: KEP-647: APIServer Tracing
Chosen: KEP-647: APIServer Tracing
Alternative considered: New EgressSelector type
Why it was not used: Existing egress types are more standard because no new traffic target is introduced, and future client configuration needs are better handled elsewhere.
Evidence: keps/sig-instrumentation/647-apiserver-tracing/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-instrumentation-647-apiserver-tracing]
Context: KEP-647: APIServer Tracing
Chosen: KEP-647: APIServer Tracing
Alternative considered: Vendoring multiple in-tree exporters
Why it was not used: This would force the Kubernetes maintainers into the unwanted role of selecting and maintaining supported tracing backends.
Evidence: keps/sig-instrumentation/647-apiserver-tracing/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-instrumentation-647-apiserver-tracing]
Context: KEP-647: APIServer Tracing
Chosen: KEP-647: APIServer Tracing
Alternative considered: Supporting both in-tree and collector exporters
Why it was not used: no reason stated in the source
Evidence: keps/sig-instrumentation/647-apiserver-tracing/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1790-recover-resize-failure]
Context: Recovery from volume expansion failure
Chosen: Recovery from volume expansion failure
Alternative considered: Tracking quota using pvc.Status.Capacity
Why it was not used: Capacity updates only after volume binding occurs, allowing users to overcommit resources before the quota reflects accurate usage.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1790-recover-resize-failure/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1790-recover-resize-failure]
Context: Recovery from volume expansion failure
Chosen: Recovery from volume expansion failure
Alternative considered: Manual administrator remediation for stuck resizing
Why it was not used: Unresolved resizes block workflows dependent on pod restarts and can render volumes unusable if node expansion continuously fails.
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1790-recover-resize-failure/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-storage-1790-recover-resize-failure]
Context: Recovery from volume expansion failure
Chosen: Recovery from volume expansion failure
Alternative considered: Restoring volume size completely to the original value
Why it was not used: no reason stated in the source
Evidence: keps/sig-storage/1790-recover-resize-failure/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-5681-conditional-authorization]
Context: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Chosen: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Alternative considered: Expose conditions in AdmissionReview for admission webhook acknowledgement
Why it was not used: Managing webhook permissions, condition dispatching, and conflicting evaluations from dynamically registered webhooks was too complex and insecure.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/5681-conditional-authorization/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-5681-conditional-authorization]
Context: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Chosen: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Alternative considered: Propagate request UID across authorization and admission
Why it was not used: This did not offer a complete long-term solution because it still depended on administrators setting up webhooks.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/5681-conditional-authorization/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-5681-conditional-authorization]
Context: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Chosen: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Alternative considered: Expose only a single ConditionSet in SubjectAccessReview status
Why it was not used: Users would not be able to discover the full set of conditional allows and denies relevant to their requests.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/5681-conditional-authorization/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-5681-conditional-authorization]
Context: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Chosen: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Alternative considered: Require clients to annotate write requests with selectors
Why it was not used: It would break existing clients, redundantly inflate payload sizes, and introduce ambiguity about whether selectors target stored or incoming objects.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/5681-conditional-authorization/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-5681-conditional-authorization]
Context: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Chosen: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
Alternative considered: Extract selectors from requests and stored objects before authorization
Why it was not used: Decoding unauthenticated bodies exposes the API server to denial-of-service attacks and makes authorization anti-pattern state-dependent.
Evidence: keps/sig-auth/5681-conditional-authorization/README.md

Decision [kep-keps-sig-auth-5681-conditional-authorization]
Context: KEP-5681: Conditional Authorization
